Dynamic Reorganization of the Frontal Parietal Network During Cognitive Control and Episodic Memory

Kimberly L Ray1, J Daniel Ragland1, Angus W MacDonald2, James M Gold3, Steven M Silverstein4, Deanna M Barch5, Cameron S Carter1,6

Cogn Affect Behav Neurosci. 2020 February ; 20(1): 76–90. doi:10.3758/s13415-019-00753-9.

None of the data or materials for the experiments reported here are available, and none of the experiments were preregistered.

Subjects

Data were obtained on 60 healthy adults (HC). Participants were excluded if they exhibited excess movement (i.e., >0.37 mm mean frame-to-frame movement), below-chance performance, or image acquisition errors. This left final samples of 56 HC (34.0±11.4 yrs) for the RiSE task, and 52 HC (34.1±10.4 yrs) for DPX task (Table 1).

Data Acquisition

Images were acquired in a single 3T MRI session using a consistent protocol across sites. Functional images were acquired using gradient-echo BOLD echo-planar imaging (TR=2000 ms, TE=30 ms, 77° flip angle, FOV=220 mm2, 3.43×3.43×4 mm voxels, 32 axial slices parallel with the anterior/posterior commissure).

Preprocessing

Pre-processing was carried out using the FMRI Expert Analysis Tool (FEAT) in the FMRIB Software Library (FSL version 4.1; www.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl) using standard procedures, including field map correction, spatial normalization and nonlinear registration to MNI152. Field maps to correct fMRI data for geometric distortion caused by magnetic field inhomogeneity and a T1-weighted anatomical image (1-mm isotropic voxels) were also acquired.

Data Processing (Beta-series regression)

Subject-wise beta-series regression analysis was performed on RiSE and DPX fMRI data in order to capture trial specific BOLD effects for each condition (Turner et al., 2012). Using the least squares-separate (LS-S) method to measure event-related functional connectivity, individual trials were modeled with a new GLM in SPM8 with two predicted BOLD time courses—one that reflects the expected BOLD response to the current event and another for the BOLD responses to all events except the current event.

Additional motion correction steps were taken analogous to data-scrubbing procedures often performed in resting-state functional connectivity analyses (Power et al., 2014). Beta-images containing frame-wise displacement (FD) values greater than 0.5mm motion were excluded from beta-series. If more than 10% of TRs within a block contained frame-wise displacement >0.5 mm, the entire block was excluded from analysis.

Parcellation and Connectivity

Next, each participant’s brain data was parcellated into discrete regions of interest representing nodes obtained from the Power atlas (Power et al., 2011). Twenty-one Power nodes were eliminated due to low signal, and two bilateral MTL nodes were added (MNI coords: −30,−12,−22;32,−14,−22) resulting with 245 nodes across the whole-brain. Beta-series pairwise correlations for all 245 nodes were extracted and z-transformed resulting with a 245 by 245 connectivity matrix. A final group FC graph for each condition was established by summing the 5% thresholded connection matrices across all subjects, then applying a subsequent 5% threshold on the summed group connection matrix to identify connections that are consistently strongest across participants, followed by binarization of the summed group connection matrix.

Graph Analysis and Measures

Modularity (Q) and modular partitions were extracted using the community Louvain algorithm provided by the Brain Connectivity Toolbox. We also quantified reorganization between high and low control using mutual information and variation of information, and examined the participation coefficient of FPN nodes.

Relational and Item-Specific Encoding (RiSE) task

Participants completed 4 encoding and 4 recognition fMRI runs. During encoding, participants alternated between 3 item-specific blocks (“Is either object living?”; 9 low cognitive control trials each) and 3 relational blocks (“Can one object fit inside the other?”; 9 high cognitive control trials each) in a jittered event-related design. During item recognition, 54 individual objects from each encoding condition (54 item-specific, 54 relational) were randomly presented with 54 new items. OPTSEQ was used to optimize the efficiency of trial presentation timing and randomization across each block.

Dot Pattern Expectancy (DPX) task

Each block consisted of 40 trials: 24 AX, 6 AY, 6 BX, and 4 BY. Cues indicated the need for high (B Cues) or low (A Cues) levels of cognitive control. Correct responses from 4 runs of the DPX task were used for analysis. OPTSEQ was used to optimize efficiency and randomization across blocks.

Ethics

Recruitment and informed consent procedures for each site were approved by their Institutional Review Boards (IRB).

Behavioral performance

As reported in Ragland et al., 2015, mean accuracy for healthy adults was 72.0% and 86.1% for item and relational recognition trials respectively.

Title: Dynamic reorganization of the frontal parietal network during cognitive control and episodic memory

Data processing and network construction
Each participant’s brain data were parcellated into discrete regions of interest obtained from the Power atlas. Twenty-one Power nodes were removed due to low signal and two bilateral medial temporal lobe nodes were added, resulting in 245 nodes across the whole brain. Beta-series pairwise correlations were computed for all nodes and Fisher z-transformed, yielding a 245 × 245 connectivity matrix.

Group functional connectivity graphs were constructed by summing the 5% thresholded individual connectivity matrices across subjects and applying a subsequent 5% threshold to identify consistently strong connections, followed by binarization.

Graph analysis
Community structure was extracted using the Louvain modularity algorithm implemented in the Brain Connectivity Toolbox. Modularity (Q) and module partitions were computed repeatedly (1,000 iterations) across proportional thresholds ranging from 0.05 to 0.60 in steps of 0.05, and the partition with the highest modularity value was retained.

Network reorganization was quantified using mutual information and variation of information between high and low cognitive-control conditions. Participation coefficient was computed to assess integration of the frontal parietal network across tasks.
